needs_result.text: Built a tool-calling LLM agent (LangChain, AWS Bedrock, Claude Haiku 4.5) for a multi-omics cancer research platform, with three tools for gene alias resolution, scoring-methodology explanation and dataset provenance.
Integrated the agent into a React front end with real-time gene alias enrichment.

Proposed the request flow: a user's text goes through the API and a customised prompt to the MCP server, where one LLM instance writes GraphQL queries against the client's Convex database and a second instance runs the statistical analysis before the result returns to the user.

Working independently for a private client, built agentic RAG workflows (LangChain, LangGraph, ChromaDB) self-hosted on the client's own server, NLP pipelines (Hugging Face Transformers, Ollama) and scikit-learn pipelines, served ML models as REST APIs (FastAPI, Docker), and contributed to a team LoRA fine-tune of a Llama model.

Designed reproducible scikit-learn pipelines with feature engineering (temporal features, interaction terms, target encoding), model selection, cross-validation and hyperparameter tuning across classification and regression tasks.
Designed Core Data schemas for user profiles, transaction histories and event bookings with CRUD and session-state management.

paragraphs: Your team will be designing solutions for complex challenges and will integrate code with software engineers. That is the kind of problem I have been working on. I check the data before I trust a model: I audited 859,494 training examples and found 44,369 duplicates, and for my AstraZeneca-affiliated MSc dissertation I combined 14 research datasets so the results rested on trusted data. When my gene models scored 0.807 on training data but only 0.545 on new data, I reported it plainly instead of hiding it.

I placed 3rd at Lloyd's Banking Group's datathon by spotting rare suspicious transactions, about 1 in 200, and in my MSc I used proper statistics, planning the sample size first and then running ANOVA tests, to pick the best of 6 algorithm settings. At 180 Degrees Consulting I helped turn a startup's vague idea into a working tool that the client now uses every day; the client's founder called it "stable, production-ready". I also built a model that predicts which bank customers are likely to leave, and I have presented results live to client stakeholders who were not technical.
Your ad asks for ai / ml solutions using a range of techniques, which is the work I want to do next.
Could we spend 20 minutes on how the team integrate code with software engineers?
